chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Makkah, so our family ate it.' He said, 'The people of Makkah do not see any problem with it.' I said, 'So what do you say?' He said, 'Upon them is its price (penalty).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating a bird slaughtered in Makkah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Ikhtilaf al-Masalik* (divergence of paths) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam distinguishes between the local customary practice (*'urf*) of the people of Makkah and the stricter religious ruling (*hukm*) applicable to the individual. While the locals deemed the slaughtered bird permissible due to their specific context, the Imam imposed a financial penalty (*thaman*) on the eaters, highlighting that personal religious obligation may exceed local custom. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's authority to define legal nuances that differ from prevailing societal norms.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Makkah, so our families ate it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The people of Makkah do not see any problem with it’. I said, ‘So which thing are you<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon them is its price (penalty)’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Flazim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a slaughtered bird given to us as gift in Makkah, if I can use it for food with my family. He (the Imam) said, ‘People of Makkah do not think it is harmful.’ I then asked, ‘What do you say about it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They owe its prices.’”
